title: Demonstrative pronouns (ça, cela, celui…)
summary: ça and cela mean 'that' or 'it' and refer to an idea, an activity or something not named; ça is everyday, cela more formal: Ça me plaît. Cela dépend.
ceci means 'this' and is mostly written: Lisez ceci attentivement.
ce is used with être; it becomes c' before e and é: C'est génial. C'était nul. Ce sont mes amis.
For a general comment, use c'est + masculine adjective: La natation, c'est bon pour la santé.
celui (masc. sing.), celle (fem. sing.), ceux (masc. pl.), celles (fem. pl.) mean 'the one(s)' and agree with the noun they replace.
celui never stands alone: it is followed by -ci (this one / these) or -là (that one / those), by qui / que, or by de: Quel pull ? Celui-ci.
celui + qui / que = the one who / that: J'ai deux frères ; celui qui joue au rugby s'appelle Tom.
celui + de shows who something belongs to: Ce n'est pas mon vélo, c'est celui de ma sœur (my sister's).

cards.front: What do ça, cela and ceci mean, and when are they used?
cards.back: ça = that / it (everyday), cela = that / it (more formal or written), ceci = this. They refer to an idea, an activity or something not named, and never change form: Ça coûte combien ? Cela m'intéresse. Ça ne fait rien.

cards.prompt: Faire du shopping avec mes parents ? Non, ___ m'énerve !
cards.en: Going shopping with my parents? No, that annoys me!
cards.why: An activity or idea is referred to with ça (or the more formal cela), not il or elle.

cards.prompt: Je voudrais un billet pour Paris. — D'accord, ___ fait quarante euros.
cards.en: I'd like a ticket to Paris. — OK, that comes to forty euros.
cards.why: ça (or cela) refers to the whole situation, here the price of what was asked for: ça fait...

cards.front: How is ce used with être?
cards.back: c'est (it is / that is), ce sont (they are / these are), c'était (it was), ce sera (it will be). ce becomes c' before e and é. For a general comment use c'est + masculine adjective: Le ski, c'est fatigant. La musique, c'est important.

cards.prompt: La natation, ___ bon pour la santé.
cards.en: Swimming is good for your health.
cards.why: A general comment about an activity uses c'est + masculine adjective: c'est bon (not elle est bonne).

cards.prompt: Regarde la photo : ___ mes cousins de Lyon.
cards.en: Look at the photo: these are my cousins from Lyon.
cards.why: Before a plural noun, written French uses ce sont rather than c'est.

cards.front: What are the four forms of celui, and what do they mean?
cards.back: celui (masc. sing.), celle (fem. sing.), ceux (masc. pl.), celles (fem. pl.) = the one / the ones. They agree with the noun they replace and must be followed by -ci / -là, qui / que or de.

cards.front: What is the difference between celui-ci and celui-là?
cards.back: -ci = this one / these (nearer), -là = that one / those (further away): Quel gâteau veux-tu ? — Celui-ci. Je préfère ces chaussures-là → je préfère celles-là.

cards.en: Which jacket do you prefer? — That one, the black one.
cards.why: veste is feminine singular, so celle; -là means 'that one'.

cards.prompt: Ces baskets-là sont trop chères. Je vais prendre ___.
cards.en: Those trainers are too expensive. I'm going to take these ones.
cards.why: baskets is feminine plural, so celles; -ci means 'these (ones)'.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a demonstrative pronoun.
cards.en: I'm going to buy this one.
cards.why: sac is masculine singular, so ce sac-ci becomes celui-ci.

cards.front: What do celui qui and celui que mean?
cards.back: The one who / that. Use qui when a verb follows, que when a subject follows: celle qui chante (the one who is singing), celui que je préfère (the one I prefer), ceux qui recyclent (those who recycle).

cards.prompt: J'ai deux sœurs : ___ qui habite à Londres s'appelle Emma.
cards.en: I have two sisters: the one who lives in London is called Emma.
cards.why: It refers to one sister (feminine singular), so celle; celle qui = the one who.

cards.prompt: J'aime bien les films d'action, mais ___ que je préfère, ce sont les comédies.
cards.en: I quite like action films, but the ones I prefer are comedies.
cards.why: It refers to films (masculine plural), so ceux; ceux que = the ones that.

cards.prompt: ___ qui fument mettent leur santé en danger.
cards.en: Those who smoke put their health at risk.
cards.why: For people in general, 'those who' is ceux qui (masculine plural).

cards.front: How do you say 'my brother's' or 'Léa's' without repeating the noun?
cards.back: celui / celle / ceux / celles + de: Ce n'est pas mon vélo, c'est celui de mon frère (my brother's). Mes notes sont meilleures que celles de Léa (Léa's). French has no 's, so de shows who owns it.

cards.instruction: Replace the words in bold with a demonstrative pronoun.
cards.prompt: Ma chambre est plus grande que **la chambre** de ma sœur.
answers: Ma chambre est plus grande que celle de ma sœur.
cards.en: My bedroom is bigger than my sister's.
cards.why: chambre is feminine singular, so la chambre de becomes celle de.

cards.prompt: Ce n'est pas mon portable, c'est ___ de Thomas.
cards.en: It's not my mobile, it's Thomas's.
cards.why: portable is masculine singular, so celui; celui de = the one belonging to.
